brief.topic: How to measure real autonomy instead of marketing autonomy
brief.audience: PMs and buyers evaluating AI agents
constraints: Example numbers labelled illustrative on screen and in caption

coreInsight: An agent’s real autonomy is measured by how often a human has to step in per task and how much time each intervention costs, not by the label on the product.

hooks.text: Count the times a human steps in.
hooks.notes: Gives the metric immediately; the reel shows how to log and read it.

hooks.text: “Fully autonomous” needs a number behind it.
hooks.notes: Good tension but doesn’t name the number.

hooks.text: Your agent is less autonomous than the demo says.

selectionRationale: Highest total (23/25): names the one measure that cuts through autonomy claims, which the checklist turns into a simple log.

scenes.purpose: State the idea so it is clear from frame 0.
scenes.onScreen: Count the times a human steps in. / That’s your agent’s real autonomy.
scenes.voiceover: Count the times a human steps in. That’s your agent’s real autonomy.

scenes.purpose: The framework: what to log for every agent task.
scenes.onScreen: THE AUTONOMY LOG / Track per task, every week. / Interventions: approvals, fixes, restarts · Minutes of human time per intervention · Share of tasks done with zero help · Split it by task type, trend it weekly / Real autonomy is the share of tasks done with no human help.
scenes.voiceover: For every task, log interventions: approvals, fixes and restarts. Log the minutes each one costs. Track the share of tasks finished with zero help. Split by task type and trend it weekly.

scenes.rule: Real autonomy is the share of tasks done with no human help.

scenes.onScreen: EXAMPLE (ILLUSTRATIVE) / The label vs the log. / THE LABEL Sold as “fully autonomous” · THE LOG 1.8 interventions per task · THE LOG 6 minutes per intervention · THE LOG 1 in 5 tasks need no help

caption.opening: “Autonomous” is a label. Interventions per task is a measurement.
body:
Log this for every agent task:
→ Interventions: approvals, fixes, restarts
→ Minutes of human time per intervention
→ Share of tasks finished with zero help
→ Split by task type, trend it weekly
Real autonomy is the share of tasks done with no human help, plus what the remaining help costs. Ask vendors for the same numbers.
(The 1.8 interventions, 6 minutes and 1-in-5 figures in the reel are illustrative, not from a real product.)

claims.text: Agent autonomy is best measured by human interventions per task, the time each costs, and the share of tasks completed without help.
1.8 interventions per task, 6 minutes per intervention, 1 in 5 tasks needing no help.
